Lagos-listed Cornerstone Plc, an insurance holding company lately acquired by Chapel Hill Denham, the investment banking firm of one of Nigeria’s most aggressive dealmakers, Bolaji Balogun, entered into a pact with rival AIICO Insurance to combine into a single entity that will create Nigeria’s largest insurer by “gross written premium, insurance revenue, and capital.”
Mr Balogun, who is the first son of the late Subomi Balogun, founder of First City Monument Bank, currently chairs Unilever Nigeria.
Two insurance subsidiaries of AIICO Insurance, the country’s biggest quoted insurer by assets, will also be folded into the surviving company.
The deal has secured approval from both companies’ boards and will now seek shareholders’ approval, Cornerstone said in a Monday regulatory filing.
“The merger would bring together two complementary insurance businesses, with combined shareholders’ funds of approximately ₦194 billion and total assets of approximately ₦858 billion,” the group said.
“On completion, the merged company will remain listed on Nigerian Exchange Limited,” it added.
Shares in Cornerstone and AIICO accelerated by 10 per cent and 9.9 per cent respectively at market close on Monday on account of the news, making them the day’s second- and third-best-performing stocks.

Chapel Hill Denham became Cornerstone’s majority owner this year in the wake of the insurance industry’s recapitalisation, snapping up a 75 per cent stake in the underwriter, a company insider who doesn’t want his identity divulged told PREMIUM TIMES.
That is worth N74.9 billion, using Cornerstone’s closing share price on Monday.
Cornerstone announced last week it had completed a transformation into a holding company after the Federal Competition and Consumer Protection Commission greenlit the move, the National Insurance Commission gave approval in principle, and the Federal High Court sanctioned the plan.
Under the new structure, subsidiary Cornerstone Life Assurance runs the group’s life insurance operations, Cornerstone General Insurance Limited (formerly FIN Insurance Company Limited) oversees its general insurance business, while Hilal Takaful Insurance Limited will continue to undertake the Group’s Takaful insurance operations.
In a statement on Monday, AIICO disclosed that Leapfrog III Nigeria Insurance Holdings, its second-biggest shareholder, agreed to offload its 30.5 per cent interest or 11.17 billion shares in the company to Insur Investments Limited, an investment vehicle sponsored by Cornerstone.
Using AIICO’s closing share price on Monday, the stake is worth N48.5 billion.
